tasks.subject: Implement Claimed Status Logic in Deal Cards
tasks.description:
Update deal card behavior so that users see a clear claimed status (e.g., “Claimed once”, “Claimed twice”) while still being able to interact with the deal until their max per user limit is reached or the deal expires.

🔧 Scope of Work
UI/UX

Add a status badge on the top‑right corner of each deal card showing claim count (e.g., “Claimed once”, “Claimed twice”).

Keep the button label as “Open Deal” (not “Claimed”) as long as:

Deal is not expired

User has not reached max per user limit

Once max per user is reached OR deal expired → button changes to disabled state with “Claimed” or “Expired”.

Logic

Track number of claims per user for each deal.

Display claim count dynamically on the badge.

Button state logic:

Open Deal → if user has claimed < max per user AND deal not expired

Claimed (disabled) → if user has claimed = max per user

Expired (disabled) → if deal expiration date passed

tasks.subject: Investigate and fix “No Available Time” Issue in Booking Flow from business app side
tasks.description:
Identify and resolve why the system is showing “no available time” when booking, by analyzing possible triggers and payload mismatches.

Possible Triggers & Problems:

Invalid service_id

Invalid assistant_id

Service exists in Firebase but no longer exists in WordPress

assistant_id: 0 not accepted by current WP install/plugin version

Specific date/time combinations trigger a plugin bug

Firestore IDs exist, but their mapped wordpress_id is missing or stale

Best Immediate Debugging Step:

Log the exact payload that WordPress receives and compare it to a known-good request.

Values to Inspect in Payload:

date

time

service_id

assistant_id

Steps to Implement:

Add detailed logging for all booking requests sent to WordPress.

Compare failing payloads with successful ones to identify discrepancies.

Validate that service_id and assistant_id are mapped correctly between Firebase and WordPress.

Check plugin version compatibility for handling assistant_id: 0.

Test multiple date/time combinations to rule out plugin bugs.

Fix stale or missing WordPress mappings for Firestore IDs.

Document findings and apply corrective measures across all environments.

tasks.subject: Add Booking Status & Revenue Analytics to Dashboard
tasks.description:
WHY WE NEED THIS
Salons currently only see booking counts (582 bookings) but can't see:

How much money they actually made (revenue)
How many customers showed up vs cancelled vs no-showed
Which bookings were profitable (marketplace vs direct)
Their completion rate and business performance

Without this data, salons can't measure business success and won't see value in upgrading to paid plans.
WHAT TO BUILD
PART 1: BOOKING STATUS SYSTEM
Add Four Status Types:

Confirmed (default when booking is created)
Completed (customer came, service done, salon earned money)
No-show (customer didn't show up)
Cancelled (customer cancelled)

Auto-Completion Logic (Calculated on Dashboard Load):
When displaying bookings on the dashboard, calculate status based on date:

If booking date is before today AND status is still "confirmed" → Display as COMPLETED
If status is manually set to "no-show" → Display as NO-SHOW
If status is "cancelled" → Display as CANCELLED
If booking date is today or future AND status is "confirmed" → Display as UPCOMING

Important: Don't update the database with calculated status. Only calculate when rendering the dashboard. The database status only changes when salon manually marks something (like marking a booking as "no-show").
Manual Status Updates:
Add a way for salons to manually change booking status in the booking list. Most important: let them mark bookings as "no-show" when customers don't show up. Make this quick and easy - add a status dropdown or buttons directly in the booking list, not buried in a details page.
PART 2: DATE RANGE FILTER
Default View:
When salon opens dashboard, show data from last 30 days by default.
Date Range Selector:
Add a date picker that lets salons choose:

Last 7 days
Last 30 days (default)
This month
Last month
Custom date range

Maximum Range:
Never allow selecting more than 90 days (3 months) at once. If salon tries to select a larger range, show error message and limit it to 90 days.
Query Optimization:
When loading dashboard data, only query bookings within the selected date range. Never load all bookings. For a salon with 88,000 total bookings, if they select "last 30 days", only query and load the ~200-500 bookings from the last 30 days.
Firebase query should filter:

salon_id equals current salon
date is greater than or equal to selected start date
date is less than or equal to selected end date

PART 3: DASHBOARD METRICS
Replace Current Simple Metric:
Current dashboard shows: "Aspio Bookings: 582"
New Dashboard Should Show:
Total Bookings Section:

Total bookings in selected period
Breakdown by source: From Marketplace (count and percentage), From Direct (count and percentage) - this requires Priority 1 task to be completed first
If Priority 1 is not done yet, just show total bookings without the breakdown

Status Breakdown:

Completed bookings (count and percentage)
Upcoming bookings (count and percentage)
No-show bookings (count and percentage)
Cancelled bookings (count and percentage)

Revenue Section:

Total Revenue from completed bookings only (sum of all completed booking amounts in SEK)
Revenue from Marketplace bookings (requires Priority 1)
Revenue from Direct bookings (requires Priority 1)
Revenue Lost from no-shows (sum of all no-show booking amounts)

Performance Metrics:

Completion Rate: Completed bookings divided by (Total minus Cancelled) times 100
No-show Rate: No-show bookings divided by (Total minus Cancelled) times 100
Average Booking Value: Total Revenue divided by Completed bookings

How to Calculate Revenue:
Only include bookings with calculated status = COMPLETED. Sum up the "amount" field from those bookings. Do not include upcoming, cancelled, or no-show bookings in revenue calculation.
PART 4: UI DESIGN
Visual Design:

Use icons for each status (✅ for completed, ❌ for no-show, 🚫 for cancelled, ⏳ for upcoming, 📍 for marketplace, 🔗 for direct)
Use colors: green for completed/positive, red for no-show/negative, gray for cancelled, purple for marketplace
Show both absolute numbers and percentages
Make it scannable - salon owners are busy and need to understand at a glance
Match existing purple Aspio design system
Ensure mobile responsive

Layout:
Organize metrics into clear sections with card-based design similar to current dashboard. Don't overwhelm with too much data - prioritize revenue and completion rate as the most important metrics.
EDGE CASES TO HANDLE

1.  Zero Bookings in Selected Period

If salon selects a date range with no bookings, show friendly message "No bookings in this period" instead of showing zeros everywhere.
2\. All Bookings Are Upcoming
If all bookings in the period are upcoming (haven't happened yet), revenue will be 0. Show "Revenue pending - all bookings are upcoming" message.
3\. Very Large Date Ranges
Enforce 90-day maximum. If salon tries to select Jan 1 to Dec 31 (365 days), show error: "Maximum date range is 90 days. Please select a shorter period."
4\. Today's Bookings
If current time is March 28 at 3:00 PM and there's a booking at March 28 at 2:00 PM with status "confirmed", treat it as UPCOMING until tomorrow (March 29). Only mark as completed when the booking date is in the past.
5\. No-Show After Date Passed
If salon marks a booking as "no-show" on March 29 for a March 28 appointment, respect the manual status. Manual status always overrides calculated status.

7\. Percentage Calculations with Zero Bookings
If total bookings is 0, avoid division by zero. Show "N/A" or "0%" for percentage metrics.
8\. Revenue Lost Calculation
Only include no-shows in revenue lost. Don't include cancelled bookings because customers cancelled in advance (salon had time to fill the slot).
9\. Dashboard Loading State
Show loading spinner or skeleton while fetching data. Don't show wrong numbers briefly before real data loads.
10\. Changing Date Range Multiple Times
If salon changes date range filter, cancel any pending data fetches and fetch fresh data for new range. Prevent showing stale data from previous range.
11\. Status Update Conflicts
If salon marks booking as "no-show" but the booking date hasn't passed yet, allow it (customer called to say they're not coming). Manual status always wins.
12\. Firebase Read Limits
With a 90-day maximum and typical salon booking volume, you'll query 500-2000 bookings max. This is safe. But add pagination if a salon somehow has 10,000+ bookings in 90 days.
13\. Booking Amount is Missing or Zero
Some old bookings might not have amount field. Treat missing amount as 0 for revenue calculations. Don't break the dashboard if amount is null.
14\. Multiple Currencies
Currently all bookings are in SEK. If you expand to other countries later, you'll need currency conversion. For now, assume all amounts are SEK.
15\. Manually Created Bookings
If salon staff creates a booking manually through the portal (phone booking), it should work the same way. Default status is "confirmed", auto-complete after date passes.
TESTING REQUIREMENTS
Test with Real Data:

Test with a salon that has 100 bookings
Test with a salon that has 50,000+ bookings
Verify dashboard loads in under 2 seconds even with large datasets

Test Different Scenarios:

All bookings completed (past dates)
Mix of upcoming, completed, no-show, cancelled
Zero bookings in selected range
Today's bookings (should show as upcoming even if time passed)

Test Date Ranges:

Last 7 days
Last 30 days
Last 90 days (maximum)
Try to select 91+ days (should be blocked)
Custom ranges with different start/end dates

Test Status Updates:

Mark upcoming booking as no-show
Mark past booking as no-show
Verify status change reflects immediately in metrics
Verify revenue recalculates correctly after status change

Test Calculations:

Manually verify revenue calculation is correct
Verify percentages add up to 100%
Verify completion rate formula is correct
Verify no-show rate formula is correct

IMPORTANT NOTES

This feature depends on Priority 1 (Booking Source Tracking) for showing marketplace vs direct revenue breakdown. You can build this feature without Priority 1 completed, but you won't be able to show the revenue split by source until Priority 1 is done.
Never load all bookings into memory. Always filter by date range in the Firebase query.
Status calculation (completed vs upcoming) happens when rendering the dashboard, NOT when creating bookings. The database doesn't store calculated status.
Manual status updates (like marking no-show) DO write to the database.
Use the salon's timezone for all date comparisons.
Revenue only counts COMPLETED bookings. Upcoming, cancelled, and no-show bookings don't contribute to revenue.

If booking date is today or future AND status is "confirmed" → Display as UPCOMING

Important: Don't update the database with calculated status. Only calculate when rendering the dashboard. The database status only changes when salon manually marks something (like marking a booking as "no-show").
Manual Status Updates:
Add a way for salons to manually change booking status in the booking list. Most important: let them mark bookings as "no-show" when customers don't show up. Make this quick and easy - add a status dropdown or buttons directly in the booking list, not buried in a details page.
PART 2: DATE RANGE FILTER
Default View:
When salon opens dashboard, show data from last 30 days by default.
Date Range Selector:
Add a date picker that lets salons choose:

Last 7 days
Last 30 days (default)
This month
Last month
Custom date range

Maximum Range:
Never allow selecting more than 90 days (3 months) at once. If salon tries to select a larger range, show error message and limit it to 90 days.
Query Optimization:
When loading dashboard data, only query bookings within the selected date range. Never load all bookings. For a salon with 88,000 total bookings, if they select "last 30 days", only query and load the ~200-500 bookings from the last 30 days.
Firebase query should filter:

salon_id equals current salon
date is greater than or equal to selected start date
date is less than or equal to selected end date

PART 3: DASHBOARD METRICS
Replace Current Simple Metric:
Current dashboard shows: "Aspio Bookings: 582"
New Dashboard Should Show:
Total Bookings Section:

Total bookings in selected period
Breakdown by source: From Marketplace (count and percentage), From Direct (count and percentage) - this requires Priority 1 task to be completed first
If Priority 1 is not done yet, just show total bookings without the breakdown

Status Breakdown:

Completed bookings (count and percentage)
Upcoming bookings (count and percentage)
No-show bookings (count and percentage)
Cancelled bookings (count and percentage)

Revenue Section:

Total Revenue from completed bookings only (sum of all completed booking amounts in SEK)
Revenue from Marketplace bookings (requires Priority 1)
Revenue from Direct bookings (requires Priority 1)
Revenue Lost from no-shows (sum of all no-show booking amounts)

Performance Metrics:

Completion Rate: Completed bookings divided by (Total minus Cancelled) times 100
No-show Rate: No-show bookings divided by (Total minus Cancelled) times 100
Average Booking Value: Total Revenue divided by Completed bookings

How to Calculate Revenue:
Only include bookings with calculated status = COMPLETED. Sum up the "amount" field from those bookings. Do not include upcoming, cancelled, or no-show bookings in revenue calculation.
PART 4: UI DESIGN
Visual Design:

Use icons for each status (✅ for completed, ❌ for no-show, 🚫 for cancelled, ⏳ for upcoming, 📍 for marketplace, 🔗 for direct)
Use colors: green for completed/positive, red for no-show/negative, gray for cancelled, purple for marketplace
Show both absolute numbers and percentages
Make it scannable - salon owners are busy and need to understand at a glance
Match existing purple Aspio design system
Ensure mobile responsive

Layout:
Organize metrics into clear sections with card-based design similar to current dashboard. Don't overwhelm with too much data - prioritize revenue and completion rate as the most important metrics.
EDGE CASES TO HANDLE

1.  Zero Bookings in Selected Period

If salon selects a date range with no bookings, show friendly message "No bookings in this period" instead of showing zeros everywhere.
2\. All Bookings Are Upcoming
If all bookings in the period are upcoming (haven't happened yet), revenue will be 0. Show "Revenue pending - all bookings are upcoming" message.
3\. Very Large Date Ranges
Enforce 90-day maximum. If salon tries to select Jan 1 to Dec 31 (365 days), show error: "Maximum date range is 90 days. Please select a shorter period."
4\. Today's Bookings
If current time is March 28 at 3:00 PM and there's a booking at March 28 at 2:00 PM with status "confirmed", treat it as UPCOMING until tomorrow (March 29). Only mark as completed when the booking date is in the past.
5\. No-Show After Date Passed
If salon marks a booking as "no-show" on March 29 for a March 28 appointment, respect the manual status. Manual status always overrides calculated status.
6\. Timezone Issues
Use consistent timezone handling. When checking if booking date is before today, use the salon's local timezone, not server timezone.
7\. Percentage Calculations with Zero Bookings
If total bookings is 0, avoid division by zero. Show "N/A" or "0%" for percentage metrics.
8\. Revenue Lost Calculation
Only include no-shows in revenue lost. Don't include cancelled bookings because customers cancelled in advance (salon had time to fill the slot).
9\. Dashboard Loading State
Show loading spinner or skeleton while fetching data. Don't show wrong numbers briefly before real data loads.
10\. Changing Date Range Multiple Times
If salon changes date range filter, cancel any pending data fetches and fetch fresh data for new range. Prevent showing stale data from previous range.
11\. Status Update Conflicts
If salon marks booking as "no-show" but the booking date hasn't passed yet, allow it (customer called to say they're not coming). Manual status always wins.
12\. Firebase Read Limits
With a 90-day maximum and typical salon booking volume, you'll query 500-2000 bookings max. This is safe. But add pagination if a salon somehow has 10,000+ bookings in 90 days.
13\. Booking Amount is Missing or Zero
Some old bookings might not have amount field. Treat missing amount as 0 for revenue calculations. Don't break the dashboard if amount is null.
14\. Multiple Currencies
Currently all bookings are in SEK. If you expand to other countries later, you'll need currency conversion. For now, assume all amounts are SEK.
15\. Manually Created Bookings
If salon staff creates a booking manually through the portal (phone booking), it should work the same way. Default status is "confirmed", auto-complete after date passes.
TESTING REQUIREMENTS
Test with Real Data:

Test with a salon that has 100 bookings
Test with a salon that has 50,000+ bookings
Verify dashboard loads in under 2 seconds even with large datasets

Test Different Scenarios:

All bookings completed (past dates)
Mix of upcoming, completed, no-show, cancelled
Zero bookings in selected range
Today's bookings (should show as upcoming even if time passed)

Test Date Ranges:

Last 7 days
Last 30 days
Last 90 days (maximum)
Try to select 91+ days (should be blocked)
Custom ranges with different start/end dates

Test Status Updates:

Mark upcoming booking as no-show
Mark past booking as no-show
Verify status change reflects immediately in metrics
Verify revenue recalculates correctly after status change

Test Calculations:

Manually verify revenue calculation is correct
Verify percentages add up to 100%
Verify completion rate formula is correct
Verify no-show rate formula is correct

IMPORTANT NOTES

This feature depends on Priority 1 (Booking Source Tracking) for showing marketplace vs direct revenue breakdown. You can build this feature without Priority 1 completed, but you won't be able to show the revenue split by source until Priority 1 is done.
Never load all bookings into memory. Always filter by date range in the Firebase query.
Status calculation (completed vs upcoming) happens when rendering the dashboard, NOT when creating bookings. The database doesn't store calculated status.
Manual status updates (like marking no-show) DO write to the database.
Use the salon's timezone for all date comparisons.
Revenue only counts COMPLETED bookings. Upcoming, cancelled, and no-show bookings don't contribute to revenue.

tasks.subject: Move SMS System from WordPress to Firebase with IP1 SMS Integration
Move SMS System from WordPress to Firebase with IP1 SMS Integration
tasks.description:
Currently WordPress controls all SMS sending (booking confirmations, cancellations, reminders). This creates problems:

-   We don't control the SMS logic
-   Can't customize SMS for new features
-   Will break when we remove WordPress booking engine
-   No visibility into SMS usage and costs per salon

We need to move SMS control to our Firebase system and integrate directly with IP1 SMS API.

## SUCCESS CRITERIA

-   [ ] Each salon can configure their own IP1 SMS credentials in settings
-   [ ] "Send Test SMS" button works and uses salon's credentials
-   [ ] Booking confirmation SMS sent immediately to customer (using salon's IP1 account)
-   [ ] Optional confirmation SMS sent to salon owner (if enabled)
-   [ ] Edit confirmation SMS sent when booking is modified
-   [ ] Cancellation SMS sent when booking is cancelled
-   [ ] Reminder SMS sent X days after service based on service settings
-   [ ] Only services with `secondary: false` get reminders (not `secondary: true`)
-   [ ] Multiple primary services get separate reminders at their own intervals
-   [ ] Salon can configure reminder period per service
-   [ ] Salon can enable/disable owner notifications
-   [ ] Dashboard shows SMS count for current month
-   [ ] SMS count resets on 1st of each month
-   [ ] All messages in Swedish
-   [ ] IP1 SMS API integrated and working with salon-specific credentials
-   [ ] Failed SMS logged but don't break bookings
-   [ ] Missing/invalid credentials handled gracefully
-   [ ] All edge cases handled gracefully
-   [ ] No duplicate reminder SMS sent

tasks.subject: Build Customer CRM System for Business App
tasks.description:
The Customers page shows only basic info with zero bookings and zero value. Salons can't see when customers last visited, track spending, identify at-risk customers, find VIPs, or view booking history. This builds a complete CRM with customer insights, segmentation, and history tracking.
ARCHITECTURE
Data flow:

Bookings stay in users/{userId}/bookings (single source of truth)
Customer stats cached in companies/{companyId}/customers/{customerId} (auto-updated via Cloud Functions)
Status and days calculated on-the-fly in frontend (no cron jobs)

Update triggers:

Booking created → Cloud Function creates/updates customer stats
Booking status/date/amount changes → Cloud Function recalculates stats
Page loads → Frontend calculates status from last_booking_date

PART 1: DATABASE CHANGES
Location: companies/{companyId}/customers/{customerId}
Remove: bookings\[] array field (broken, delete completely)
Add new fields:
stats object:

last_booking_date, first_booking_date (ISO date or null)
last_booking_service (string or null)
last_service_ids (array of last 3 service IDs)
total_bookings, completed_bookings, upcoming_bookings, cancelled_bookings, no_show_bookings (numbers)
total_spent, average_booking_value (SEK amounts)
preferred_staff_id (most frequently booked staff, or null)

Other fields:

tags (array of strings like \["VIP", "Regular"])
marketing_opt_out (boolean - true means can't receive marketing SMS)
internal_notes (string for private salon notes)
stats_last_updated (timestamp)

IMPORTANT: Do NOT store days_since_last_visit or status - calculate these in frontend

PART 2: CLOUD FUNCTIONS
onBookingCreated
Trigger: New booking in users/{userId}/bookings
Does: Check if customer exists for this company → if not, create → update stats
onBookingUpdated
Trigger: Booking updated in users/{userId}/bookings
Does: Check if status/date/amount changed → if yes, recalculate stats
Helper: findOrCreateCustomer
Does: Search for customer by user_uid → if not found, create new customer with data from users collection → return customer reference
Helper: updateCustomerStats
Does:

Fetch all user's bookings from users/{userId}/bookings
Filter for this company only (by company_id)
Categorize by status and date (completed = past + confirmed, upcoming = future + confirmed, cancelled, no-show)
Calculate: total_spent (sum completed amounts), average_booking_value, counts
Find last/first booking dates, last service name, last 3 service IDs
Calculate preferred staff (most frequent staff_id)
Update customer document with stats object

PART 3: FRONTEND STATUS CALCULATION
When page loads, calculate for each customer:
Status logic (priority order):

If total_spent ≥ 5000 SEK OR total_bookings ≥ 15 → "vip"
If total_bookings ≤ 1 OR no last_booking_date → "new"
Calculate days since last_booking_date
If upcoming_bookings > 0 AND days > 30 → "active" (has future booking)
If days ≤ 30 → "active"
If days 31-90 → "at_risk"
If days > 90 → "inactive"

Days calculation:

Difference between last_booking_date and today in days

Enrich customers:

Add days_since_last_visit and status to each customer object
Use enriched data for display and filtering
Never write these back to database

PART 4: CUSTOMER TABLE UI
Columns:

Checkbox (bulk selection)
Status Badge ( Active,  At Risk, 🔴 Inactive, ⭐ VIP, 🆕 New)
Name (first + last)
Contact (email line 1, phone line 2)
Last Visit ("X days ago" + service name)
Bookings (total with tooltip showing breakdown)
Lifetime Value (total_spent SEK)
Actions (View, SMS, Edit icons)

Filter Tabs:

All, Active, At Risk, Inactive, VIP, New, No Phone (with counts)
Calculate counts by filtering enriched customers
Filter customers when tab clicked

Search:

Search first_name, last_name, email, phone, tags
Case insensitive
Works with tab filters

Sort options:

Last visit (newest/oldest)
Name (A-Z, Z-A)
Lifetime value (high/low)
Total bookings (most/least)

Bulk Actions:

When customers selected, show bar with: Send SMS, Add Tag, Export CSV, Delete
Export includes: Name, Email, Phone, Status, Last Visit, Bookings, Value

PART 5: CUSTOMER DETAIL VIEW
Open: Side panel or modal when clicking View icon
Header:

Status badge
Name, email, phone
Tags (clickable pills, X to remove, + to add)
Marketing toggle (can receive SMS checkbox)
Edit/SMS/Close buttons

Stats Cards (2x4 grid):

Row 1: Total Bookings, Completed, Upcoming, Lifetime Value
Row 2: First Visit, Last Visit (days ago), Avg Booking, Preferred Staff

Booking History:

Fetch from users/{user_uid}/bookings filtered by company_id
Sort newest first
Show: date, time, service, staff, amount, status icon
Paginate (10 per page, Load More button)
Export CSV button

Internal Notes:

Display internal_notes field (parse line breaks)
Add note: textarea + Save button
Format: "\[timestamp - user] note text"
Append to existing notes

Quick Actions:

Book Appointment (pre-fill customer)
Send SMS (pre-fill phone)
Edit Customer (update name/email/phone)

PART 6: TAGS SYSTEM
Pre-defined tags: VIP, Regular, New Customer, High Value, At Risk
Custom tags: Salons create unlimited tags (e.g. "Sensitive skin", "Always late", "Student")
UI:

Detail view shows tags as pills
Click X to remove
Click + Add Tag → dropdown with existing tags + create new
Uses Firestore arrayUnion/arrayRemove



EDGE CASES

No user_uid: Show warning, disable booking history, provide Fix Link button
User deleted: Show "User deleted" badge, disable SMS/booking, keep historical stats
500+ bookings: Paginate history, don't load all at once
Stats calc fails: Log error, don't crash booking flow, show "stats outdated" warning
No amount: Skip booking in financial calcs, don't crash
No phone: Show "No Phone" badge, disable SMS, prompt to add
No name: Show email or "Unnamed Customer"
Multiple companies: Each has separate customer record, stats filtered by company_id
No bookings: Show all stats as 0, status "new", allow deletion

TESTING CHECKLIST
Cloud Functions:

Create booking → customer auto-created, stats updated
Update status → stats recalculated
Works with missing data

Frontend Table:

Loads fast (< 5s for 1000 customers)
Status badges correct
All filters work
Search finds customers
Sort works

Detail View:

Opens correctly
Stats accurate
Booking history from users collection
Tags add/remove
Notes save
Marketing toggle works

Migration:

Backfill populates all stats
Cleanup removes old field
Orphans fixed or logged

SUCCESS CRITERIA

Table shows status, last visit, bookings, value
Filters work (All, Active, At Risk, Inactive, VIP, New, No Phone)
Search and sort work
Detail view shows full history
Tags and notes functional
Stats auto-update on booking changes
All customers backfilled
Page loads < 5s with 1000 customers

IMPLEMENTATION ORDER

Backend: Helper functions → Cloud Functions → Deploy → Test
Migration: Backfill → Cleanup → Fix orphans
Frontend Table: Status calc → Table → Filters → Search/Sort
Frontend Detail: Panel → Stats → History → Tags → Notes
Testing & Launch: Test → Fix → Deploy → Monitor

Sort newest first

Run once after deploying Cloud Functions

Run once after backfill

Stats accurate
Booking history from users collection

Cleanup removes old field
Orphans fixed or logged

Search and sort work
Detail view shows full history
Tags and notes functional
Stats auto-update on booking changes
All customers backfilled
Page loads < 5s with 1000 customers

tasks.subject: Schema & Core Logic Setup
tasks.description:
Establish the foundational metadata and query logic for the Soft Delete (Trash) and Restore system in Firestore.

Steps:

**Add Metadata Fields**

**Introduce standardized fields across all Firestore collections**:

is_deleted (Boolean)

status (String)

deletedAt (Timestamp)

trashedByUserId (String)

Implement Null‑Coalescing Logic

Treat records with is_deleted = null or false as active.

Only set is_deleted = true when a user initiates a delete action.

Avoid bulk backfill to minimize Firebase read/write costs.

**Update Queries**

**Refactor all marketplace and public‑facing queries to exclude trashed items**:

javascript
.where('is_deleted', '!=', true)

tasks.subject: Synchronization & Multi‑Platform Flow, Establish Metadata & Query Logic for Soft Delete
tasks.description:
Ensure consistent soft delete state synchronization between Firestore, WordPress, and the Aspio ecosystem across Web and Mobile platforms.

Lay the groundwork for the Trash/Restore system in Firestore.

Steps:

WordPress Sync Configuration

Replace DELETE commands with PUT/PATCH requests to update WordPress item status to 'trash'.

Confirm that status changes propagate correctly to the external booking engine.

Implement error handling and logging for failed sync attempts.

Web (Next.js) Integration

Update the business_web API to handle soft delete and restore operations.

Ensure queries and mutations respect the new is_deleted and status fields.

Add middleware to enforce validation rules before sending updates to WordPress.

**Mobile (Flutter) Implementation**

Enable direct interaction with Firestore for soft delete actions.

Use Cloud Functions as a proxy to forward WordPress sync requests.

Ensure parity with Web logic so mobile users see consistent Trash/Restore behavior.

tasks.subject: Validation & Safety Rules
tasks.description:
Ensure safe deletion practices and restrict access to sensitive Trash Bin operations.

Steps:

Booking Validation

Block trashing of staff/services with upcoming bookings (pending or confirmed).

Category Validation

Prevent deletion of categories containing active services.

Customer Validation

Restrict customer deletion if they have future appointments.

Firestore Security Rules

Limit Trash Bin access to Salon Owners/Managers only.

Enforce role‑based permissions for restore, permanent delete.

Add audit logging for accountability.

tasks.subject: Trash Bin UI & Lifecycle Management
tasks.description:
Provide a user‑friendly interface for managing trashed items and controlling their lifecycle.

Steps:

**UI Development**

Build Trash Bin dashboards in Web (Next.js) and Mobile (Flutter).

Ensure dashboards are accessible only to authorized roles.

**Restore Functionality**

Implement logic to flip is_deleted = false and status = "published".

Confirm restored items reappear in queries and UI.

**Permanent Delete**

Implement irreversible hard wipe from Firestore and WordPress.

Add confirmation prompts to prevent accidental deletion.

tasks.subject: Fix 404 Page language flicker UX
tasks.description:
When a not-logged-in user opens the 404 page, the content first appears in Swedish and then quickly switches to English.

This language flicker creates a poor user experience.

Additionally, the navigation bar behaves unstably during this transition.

Expected Behavior:

The 404 page should load directly in the correct language (English for default, or based on user/browser settings).

Navigation should remain smooth, stable and consistent without flickering or layout shifts.

tasks.subject: Improve Broken Link Handling on Booking Page
tasks.description:
When accessing <https://app.aspio.io/booking/new-booking-compay-est> (with a typo in the URL), the page loads without any indication that the link is invalid.

Users who mistype or alter the URL are not informed that the page is broken, which creates confusion and poor UX.

Instead of showing a clear error state, the system behaves as if the page exists but with no meaningful feedback.

Expected Behavior:

The system should detect invalid or malformed booking URLs.

A proper error message or 404 page should be displayed, clearly informing the user that the link is broken.

The error page should provide helpful next steps (e.g., return to homepage, retry booking, or contact support).

tasks.subject: Investigate Missing Services in "Near You" Results
tasks.description:
The “Service Near You” feature does not consistently display all nearby services.

Example: Nuhas, Elnzo, and Salon Solis are located in Addis Ababa but are not shown in the “Near You” list.

Other services in the same area do appear, so the filtering logic seems inconsistent.

This creates confusion for users and reduces trust in the feature.

Expected Behavior:

All services within the defined proximity (e.g., Addis Ababa) should be displayed in the “Near You” section.

Results should be consistent and predictable, with no missing entries for valid businesses.

tasks.subject: Handle Invalid Deal Links Gracefully
tasks.description:
When accessing a valid deal link (e.g., <https://app.aspio.io/deals/Bav6Lpyu5A1Qx5ugtiHs>) and then deleting 1–2 characters from the URL, the page shows a shimmer/loading state as if the deal is coming.

This misleads users into thinking the content is loading, instead of clearly indicating that the link is broken or invalid.

The lack of feedback creates confusion and poor UX.

Expected Behavior:

Invalid or malformed deal links should not trigger a shimmer/loading state.

Instead, the system should display a clear error message or a custom “Deal Not Found” page.

The error page should provide helpful next steps (e.g., return to deals list, go back to homepage, or contact support).

tasks.subject: Add Category to Deals Detail Page
tasks.description:
The current deals detail page does not display the category of the deal.

Users may find it difficult to understand the context or type of deal without this information.

tasks.subject: Update Category Icon & Investigate Saved Deals Expiry, claimed deals
tasks.description:
Problem 1 (Category Icon):

The category icon on the deals detail page does not match the design used in the APK version.

This creates inconsistency across platforms and may confuse users.

Problem 2 (Saved Deals Expiry):

In the “Saved Deals” tab, expired deals remain visible even after the 24-hour time limit has passed.

This misleads users into thinking the deal is still valid and it even **shows up on changed location**.

Expected Behavior:

Saved deals should automatically expire and be removed or marked as inactive once the 24-hour countdown has passed.

The tab should only show active, valid deals.

The category icon should be updated to match the APK design for consistency and better recognition.

tasks.subject: Deals Page and other pages Naming, Tabs, and Search Bar Structure
tasks.description:
The current deals page layout lacks clarity in naming conventions, tab organization, and search bar placement.

Users may struggle to navigate or quickly find deals due to inconsistent structure.

Expected Behavior:

Page naming should be intuitive and consistent with the rest of the platform.

Tabs should be clearly labeled and logically grouped (e.g., Active Deals, Saved Deals, Expired Deals).

The search bar should be placed in a prominent, user-friendly location (e.g., top of the page or within the tab header).

The phrasing should be friendlier and more conversational.

Not yet used (instead of “0 times”)

Used once (instead of “1 time”)

Used twice (instead of “2 times”)

Used X times (for 3 or more)

Password Field

Confirm Password Field

Inline error if mismatch occurs.

UI/UX is consistent across all placements.

tasks.subject: Redesign Business App Dashboard

Total bookings metric appears twice.

Some cards are large, while others are small, creating visual imbalance.

Overall design lacks cohesion and clarity.

Card Consistency

Standardize card sizes for metrics (same height/width).

Ensure alignment and spacing are uniform across the dashboard.

Optionally, allow cards to be expandable/collapsible for detailed views.

Information Hierarchy

Remove duplicate metrics (e.g., total bookings shown twice).

Prioritize key KPIs (bookings, revenue, active users) at the top.

Secondary metrics can be grouped or placed in expandable sections.

Visual Design

Apply a consistent color palette and typography.

Use icons or subtle graphics to differentiate card types.

Maintain clean, minimal design with plenty of whitespace.

User Experience

Dashboard should be easy to scan at a glance.

Cards should be interactive (expand for more details, hover effects).

Ensure responsiveness across desktop, tablet, and mobile.

tasks.subject: Research (Compliance + Technical Requirements)
tasks.description:
Regulatory Compliance

GDPR: Consent must be explicit, informed, revocable. “Deny” must be as visible as “Allow.”

ePrivacy Directive: Requires prior consent for non-essential cookies.

CCPA: Must allow opt-out of data “sale” (maps to advertising cookies).

Audit trail: Consent choices must be logged and retrievable.

Best Practices

Three-button model: Deny, Allow selection, Allow all.

Equal prominence for all buttons.

Accordion-style categories:

Necessary (always on)

Analytics

Advertising/Targeting

Category descriptions: Marketing team provides clear, user-friendly text (with formatting support).

Multilingual support: Banner text and category descriptions translatable.

Technical Considerations

Scripts injected conditionally based on consent:

Admin settings: Fields for data-website-id and script management.

Support both cookie-based and cookieless tracking (Datafa.st).

Proxy integration for analytics scripts.

Compatibility with Microsoft Clarity, Meta Pixel, LinkedIn Pixel.

Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 compliance.

tasks.subject: Implement Cookie Consent (Necessary & Marketing Cookies)

tasks.subject: Design campaign modal/drawer
tasks.description:
Design campaign modal/drawer:

Section 1: Select Recipients (filters + live count).

Section 2: Create Message (templates, text field, variables, preview).

Section 3: Review & Send (summary card, test send, send now, schedule).

Progress states (sending, success, scheduled).

Mobile responsive design (full-screen modal, collapsible filters, stacked buttons).

### Campaign Modal/Drawer Design

**When owner clicks "Send SMS Campaign":**

Open large modal or side drawer with these sections:

**Section 1: Select Recipients**

-   Use same filter UI as Customer CRM page
-   Show live count: "238 customers match filters"
-   Note: "7 customers excluded (opted out)"

**Section 2: Create Message**

-   Template selector (dropdown or grid)
-   Message text field (large textarea)
-   Character counter
-   Variable insertion dropdown
-   "Include booking link" checkbox
-   Preview below

**Section 3: Review & Send**

-   Summary card (recipients, SMS count, cost)
-   Test send button (optional)
-   Send Now button (primary)
-   Schedule for Later button (secondary)
-   Cancel button

**Progress states:**

-   While sending: Show progress bar or spinner
-   "Sending... 45 / 238 sent"
-   Don't allow closing modal during send

**Success state:**

-   After sending: Show success message
-   "✓ Campaign sent to 238 customers (476 SMS)"
-   Link to view in campaign history
-   Close modal automatically after 3 seconds or let owner close

**Scheduled state:**

-   After scheduling: Show success message
-   "✓ Campaign scheduled for March 28, 10:00 AM"
-   "You can cancel this campaign from Campaign History"

tasks.subject: Research (Compliance + Technical Requirements)
tasks.description:
Regulatory Compliance

GDPR: Consent must be explicit, informed, revocable. “Deny” must be as visible as “Allow.”

ePrivacy Directive: Requires prior consent for non-essential cookies.

CCPA: Must allow opt-out of data “sale” (maps to advertising cookies).

Audit trail: Consent choices must be logged and retrievable.

Best Practices

Three-button model: Deny, Allow selection, Allow all.

Equal prominence for all buttons.

Accordion-style categories:

Necessary (always on)

Analytics

Advertising/Targeting

Category descriptions: Marketing team provides clear, user-friendly text (with formatting support).

Multilingual support: Banner text and category descriptions translatable.

Technical Considerations

Scripts injected conditionally based on consent:

Admin settings: Fields for data-website-id and script management.

Support both cookie-based and cookieless tracking (Datafa.st).

Proxy integration for analytics scripts.

Compatibility with Microsoft Clarity, Meta Pixel, LinkedIn Pixel.

Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 compliance.

tasks.subject: Update Calendar Day Selection with Staff & Service Integration
tasks.description:
Enhance the calendar booking workflow so that when a user selects a day, the system automatically fills in the time, assigns staff from the selected column, and then allows the user to choose a service.

Scope
Calendar Day Selection

When a user clicks on a day in the calendar, the selected date should update immediately.

Default time slot should be auto‑filled based on availability rules (e.g., first available slot).

User can override/change the time if needed.

Staff Assignment

Staff should be automatically selected based on the column chosen in the calendar view.

Ensure correct mapping between calendar column and staff profile.

Staff selection should be editable if the user wants to reassign.

Service Selection

After staff is auto‑selected, user chooses the service from a dropdown or list.

Service options should be filtered based on staff capabilities (only services that staff can perform).

Interaction Flow

User selects a day → calendar updates.

Time auto‑filled → editable by user.

Staff auto‑selected from column → editable.

User chooses service → filtered by staff.

Technical Considerations

Ensure time zone consistency (no offset errors).

Validate staff availability before confirming booking.

Handle edge cases: double bookings, blocked times, staff unavailability.

Deliverables

Updated calendar component with auto‑fill logic.

Staff‑column mapping integration.

Service selection dropdown with filtering.

QA checklist for booking flows (single booking, staff reassignment, service filtering).

Acceptance Criteria:
✅ When an access token is within a defined threshold of expiring (e.g., 5 minutes), a background refresh request is triggered automatically

✅ The refresh logic handles edge cases — if the refresh token is expired/invalid(24 hours), the user is then logged out gracefully with a clear session-expired message
✅ No unexpected or silent logouts occur during an active user session
✅ Token refresh behavior is covered by unit/integration tests

tasks.subject: List Every Feature and Module of the Business App with Functionality
tasks.description:
Both developers must sit together and produce a complete written list of every feature and module currently in the Aspio business app. This includes everything visible in the sidebar and dashboard — booking system, services, calendar, staff, customers, deals, journal, loyalty card, discounts, settings, site editor, social links, and marketing campaigns — as well as any hidden, partial, or in‑progress features. For each module, the functionality must be described clearly (what it does, why it exists, and how it works). This list will serve as the foundation for all future mapping and restructuring tasks.

Priority: High

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ A written document lists every feature and module currently in the business app with no omissions.

✅ Each feature/module includes a functionality description (e.g., “Booking system: allows customers to schedule appointments, manage cancellations, and view availability”).

✅ Both developers have reviewed and agreed on the list together — not done individually.

✅ Any partial, hidden, or coming‑soon features are clearly labeled as such.

✅ Document is saved and shared in the team workspace.

Examples of Functionality to Capture:

Booking System: Customers schedule, cancel, and reschedule appointments.

Services: Manage service offerings, pricing, and descriptions.

Calendar: Displays staff availability and upcoming bookings.

Staff: Manage staff profiles, restrictions, and availability.

Customers: Store customer data, history, and preferences.

Deals: Create and manage promotional offers.

Journal: Track customer notes, edits, and original entries.

Loyalty Card: Reward system for repeat customers.

Discounts: Apply percentage or fixed discounts to services.

Settings: Configure app behavior, restrictions, and preferences.

Site Editor: Customize business website layout and content.

Social Links: Connect business app to social media accounts.

Marketing Campaigns: Manage SMS/email campaigns and payments.

tasks.subject: Identify Every Database Entity Used by the Business App
tasks.description:
Both developers must go through the Firebase database and list every collection that the business app reads from or writes to. For each entity, they must note whether it belongs to the business app only, the marketplace only, or is shared between both. This is critical because the two apps share one database — understanding ownership at the entity level prevents cross‑app bugs and ensures safe planning for future features. Reference known collections such as companies, users, bookings, asplo\_products, crm\_deals, journal, staff, and any others found.

Priority: High

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Every Firebase collection touched by the business app is listed with its name and purpose.

✅ Each entity is labeled: business‑only, marketplace‑only, or shared.

✅ Key fields of each entity are noted (not full schema — just the fields that matter for relationships).

✅ Both developers have reviewed and agreed on the list together.

✅ Document is saved and shared in the team workspace.

tasks.subject: Draw the Full Relationship Map on Paper
tasks.description:
Using the outputs from Feature & Module List and Database Entities, both developers must sit together and draw the architecture map on paper. The map must show:

Which features connect to which database entities

How entities relate to each other (foreign keys, dependencies, triggers)

Where the business app connects to the marketplaceEvery connection must be labeled with its type — reads, writes, depends on, or triggers. This is the most important thinking exercise in the epic. AI tools may be used to structure notes, but all mapping logic must come directly from the developers. The paper drawing must be photographed and submitted as a deliverable.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ A physical paper drawing exists showing features, entities, and their connections.

✅ Every connection on the map has a label indicating its type (reads / writes / depends on / triggers).

✅ The boundary between business app and marketplace is clearly marked.

✅ A clear photo of the drawing is uploaded and shared with the PM before this task is closed.

✅ Both developers contributed to the drawing in the same session.

tasks.subject: Digitize the Map into a Clean Architecture Diagram
tasks.description:
Transfer the paper drawing from Task‑03 into a digital diagramming tool such as Figma, Miro, Lucidchart, or draw\.io. The digital version must be clean, readable, and complete — not just a digital copy of the paper but a refined version that someone who wasn’t part of the process can understand. It must clearly show:

All entities and their relationships

Which features connect to which data

The business app vs marketplace boundaries

The direction of all dependencies (reads, writes, depends on, triggers)
This diagram will serve as the permanent reference for the team going forward.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ A digital diagram exists that matches and refines the paper drawing.

✅ All entities, features, relationships, and boundaries are visible and labeled.

✅ Dependency direction is shown with arrows (not just lines).

✅ The diagram is readable by someone who did not participate in creating it.

✅ A shareable link or exported file is saved in the team workspace.

tasks.subject: PM Review Session, Identify Gaps, Risks, and Open Questions
tasks.description:
We review the digital diagram together with both developers in a dedicated session. The goal is not to fix everything immediately but to surface what is unclear, missing, or risky. During this session, flag:

Any features or entities that are undocumented or ambiguous

Any shared entities between business app and marketplace that could cause cross‑app bugs

Any entity or relationship that has no clear owner

All findings must be logged as separate tasks in Hubstaff. This session closes only when all gaps are either resolved or formally logged.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ PM and both developers have reviewed the diagram together in a live session.

✅ A gap list is produced documenting anything missing, unclear, or risky.

✅ All gaps are either resolved during the session or logged as individual follow‑up tasks in Hubstaff.

✅ Risk flags (shared entities with no clear owner, undocumented connections) are clearly noted.

tasks.subject: Approve and Maintain Architecture Diagram as Source of Truth
tasks.description:
Close the epic with a final version of the architecture diagram that incorporates all feedback from Task‑05 (PM Review Session). Both developers and the PM must formally agree that this diagram is the single source of truth for the Aspio business app architecture. Equally important: the team must agree on a going‑forward rule — every new feature or task that touches the architecture must update this diagram before development starts. The diagram must be pinned and accessible to the whole team at any time, not buried in a folder.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ The final diagram incorporates all corrections and additions from the other tasks review.

✅ Everone has formally signed off on the diagram as complete and accurate.

✅ Both developers have confirmed the diagram reflects reality as they understand it.

✅ The team has agreed in writing (message or doc) that the diagram will be updated with every new feature going forward.

The main dashboard has a few English card titles, subtitles, and buttons mixed into an otherwise Swedish screen.

The button inside the onboarding checklist step for choosing a website name (currently Select name)
The top-left stat card: its title and its subtitle
The bottom-right stat card: its title, the two lines describing top-up status, and its button
The button under "Snabbåtgärder" / "Redigera webbplats" (currently Go to Editor)

Remove the emoj after creating a company 

✅ Acceptance Criteria

✅ Onboarding checklist button is in Swedish
✅ Top-left stat card (title + subtitle) is fully in Swedish
✅ Bottom-right stat card (title, both status lines, button) is fully in Swedish
✅ "Snabbåtgärder" button is in Swedish
✅ Dashboard checked in both empty state (all values at 0, no activity) and a populated state to confirm no English string only appears once data exists

tasks.subject: Payment  Plans translation
tasks.description:
The plan comparison cards and the "Plan details" modal have the most English text of any screen  section headers, row labels, and status text throughout.

The link shown under each plan's button on the comparison list (currently View full details)
The modal's header and subtitle when it opens
The status pill next to the plan name at the top of the modal (currently ACTIVE)
The line showing billing currency, near the top of the modal
Every section header inside the modal (there are five: one above included/excluded features, one above monthly price/startup fee, one for billing dates, and one for current usage)
Every row label inside those sections (monthly price, startup fee, period start/end, usage reset date, grace period)
The small grey "used this period" text shown under each included feature

Acceptance Criteria

✅ "View full details" link on every plan card is in Swedish
✅ Modal header, subtitle, and status pill are in Swedish
✅ All five section headers inside the modal are in Swedish
✅ All row labels under those sections are in Swedish
✅ "Used this period" text is in Swedish for every included feature, at 0 and at higher usage counts
✅ Modal re-checked on both a paid plan and the free plan to confirm nothing is plan-specific and missed

✅ UI/UX optimized for mobile usability.

✅ Stakeholders approve design.

tasks.subject: Fix Duration Display in Booking & Service Detail Pages
tasks.description:
Currently, the Booking Detail page and Service Detail page show duration as empty, while the Booking List and Service List pages correctly display the duration. Update logic so that duration is consistently shown across all detail views.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ UI provides clear feedback during creation.

✅ QA confirms smooth functionality across devices.

tasks.description:
Currently, the AI Studio allows creation of deals and loyalty cards but does not support reading existing ones. Add functionality to fetch and display existing deals and loyalty cards from the database.

tasks.subject: Fix Typing & UI in AI Studio
tasks.description:
Enhance the Aspio AI Studio UI by fixing issues with typing behavior and UI inconsistencies, especially around the robot interaction area and the fonts used in generated images. The goal is to ensure smooth typing, consistent font rendering, and polished UI/UX.

✅ Typing in robot area works smoothly.

✅ Fonts in generated images are consistent and readable.

✅ QA confirms UI/UX improvements across devices.

tasks.subject: Implement Telegram Messaging for Booking Notifications in Ethiopia
tasks.description:
Add Telegram integration to the Aspio Business App so that customers and business owners in Ethiopia receive booking notifications via Telegram messages instead of SMS. This ensures reliable communication in regions where SMS delivery is limited or costly.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Customers and owners in Ethiopia receive booking notifications via Telegram.

✅ Telegram integration works seamlessly with booking flow.

✅ QA confirms fallback to SMS when Telegram is not linked.

tasks.subject: Telegram Bot Integration for Salons
tasks.description:
Integrate Telegram Bot functionality into the Aspio Business App so salons can receive real‑time booking notifications directly in Telegram. Salons should be able to connect their Telegram account, group, or channel to their Aspio account. Notifications should include key booking details and trigger instantly when a booking is created, cancelled, rescheduled, or updated. This helps salon owners and staff respond quickly without constantly monitoring the Aspio dashboard.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Salons can connect Telegram accounts/groups/channels to Aspio.

✅ Notifications sent instantly for booking creation, cancellation, reschedule, and update.

✅ Notifications include key booking details.

✅ QA confirms consistent behavior across salon accounts.

tasks.subject: Show Out‑of‑Hours Bookings on Calendar
tasks.description:
Update the Aspio Business App so that bookings made outside of configured working hours (e.g., 7 PM or 6 PM) are still visible on the calendar. Currently, bookings outside business hours may not display, which reduces visibility for staff and owners.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Out‑of‑hours bookings display on calendar.

✅ Bookings remain editable and manageable.

✅ QA confirms consistent behavior across roles and devices.

tasks.subject: Implement Trusted Review Eligibility and Submission Operations
tasks.description:
Build backend logic to enforce review eligibility rules and handle review submissions atomically. This ensures reviews are only created for valid bookings and prevents duplicates.

Requirements:

Verify booking ownership, company association, and status.

Enforce 24‑hour grace period and 30‑day review window.

Block reviews for cancelled or no‑show bookings.

Ensure atomic creation of review record and company rating aggregation.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Only eligible bookings can create reviews.

✅ Duplicate reviews are prevented.

✅ Company aggregates update correctly.

tasks.subject: Review UI & Customer Flow
tasks.description:
Design and implement the review flow in the customer app, including entry points from My Bookings → History, the Reviews menu, and notifications.

Requirements:

Show “Leave a review” on eligible bookings.

Add “Awaiting your review” and “Your reviews” sections.

Implement notification triggers (immediate after Completed, 24h after unresolved).

Include rating (1–5 stars), optional feedback, and booking snapshot details.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Customers can submit reviews from eligible bookings.

✅ Notifications trigger correctly.

✅ Review form captures rating and feedback with booking details.

tasks.subject: Company Response & Moderation Tools
tasks.description:
Provide businesses with tools to respond to reviews and report inappropriate or disputed reviews. Ensure moderation workflow is supported.

Requirements:

Allow one public company reply per review.

Enable editing/removal of company replies.

Add reporting options (abuse, irrelevant, appointment did not occur).

Ensure reported reviews are flagged for moderation without automatic removal.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Companies can reply to reviews.

✅ Companies can report reviews for moderation.

✅ Reported reviews are flagged and handled correctly.

tasks.subject: Online prepayment / deposits at booking
tasks.description:
As a salon owner, I want to require a deposit or full prepayment when a client books, so that I reduce no-shows and secure revenue upfront.

Prerequisites:

Confirm the current payment provider supports held/captured payments and partial refunds
Decide default cancellation-policy windows (how late is "late"?)
Legal/ToS text updated to cover prepayment and refund terms

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Salon owner can set a payment policy per service: no payment required, deposit (fixed amount or %), or full prepayment
✅ Customer sees the required payment amount before confirming a booking
✅ Customer can pay by card at the time of booking (reuse existing payment integration)
✅ Booking only confirms once payment succeeds; a failed payment blocks the booking
✅ Salon owner can see which bookings are prepaid/deposited vs. unpaid, in the calendar and booking list
✅ A refund flow exists for cancellations within the salon's own cancellation policy window
✅ The transaction fee is applied and visible in the salon's payout report

tasks.subject: Google Pay / Apple Pay at checkout
tasks.description:
As a customer, I want to pay with Google Pay or Apple Pay at checkout, so that I can book faster without typing card details.

Prerequisites:

Confirm the current payment processor's SDK supports Google Pay and Apple Pay
Apple Pay requires an Apple Developer Merchant ID and domain verification — needs setting up in advance
Google Pay requires merchant registration with the Google Pay API

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Google Pay appears as a payment option on supported Android devices/browsers
✅ Apple Pay appears as a payment option on supported iOS devices/Safari
✅ Both only show when the device/browser supports them; falls back to card entry otherwise
✅ A successful payment via either method confirms the booking exactly like a card payment
✅ Payment reconciles correctly in the salon owner's payout reports — no separate reporting path needed

tasks.subject: Online product store
tasks.description:
As a salon owner, I want to sell my retail products online, so that regular clients can reorder without visiting in person.

Prerequisites:

Retail/POS + inventory feature must ship first — hard dependency
Decide fulfillment policy: does Aspio only handle payment, or also shipping/logistics guidance?

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Salon owner can list products for sale online (name, price, image, description, stock count)
✅ Customers can browse and purchase products via the salon's Aspio profile/marketplace page
✅ Stock count decreases automatically on purchase; out-of-stock items are hidden or marked unavailable
✅ Salon owner gets order notifications and can mark orders as fulfilled/shipped
✅ Purchases appear in the salon's revenue reporting alongside service revenue

tasks.subject: Memberships & packages
tasks.description:
As a salon owner, I want to sell recurring memberships and prepaid session packages, so that I generate predictable recurring revenue.

Prerequisites:

Decide on a recurring-billing engine: build in-house vs. use the payment provider's subscriptions product (e.g. Stripe Billing)
Decide proration and cancellation rules for memberships
Confirm compliance with EU Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) rules for recurring card charges

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Salon owner can create a package (e.g. "5 facials for X kr") with a defined number of sessions and optional expiry
✅ Salon owner can create a recurring membership plan (e.g. "Unlimited blowouts, billed monthly") with auto-renewal
✅ Customer can purchase a package/membership from the salon's booking page
✅ Booking flow automatically deducts a session from an active package, or checks membership validity, instead of charging again
✅ Membership auto-renews and auto-charges the saved payment method each billing cycle
✅ Customer can view their remaining sessions / membership status in their own account
✅ Salon owner can cancel or pause a customer's membership
✅ A failed renewal payment triggers a retry and notifies both customer and salon owner

tasks.subject: Video consultation
tasks.description:
As a customer, I want to book a video call instead of an in-person visit for consultation-type services, so that I can get advice without traveling to the salon.

Prerequisites:

Pick and contract a video call SDK (e.g. Daily, Twilio Video, Whereby embed) — short technical spike recommended first
If used for regulated categories (e.g. medical/psychologist consultations), review GDPR/data-handling requirements before building

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Salon owner can mark a service as "video consultation" instead of in-person
✅ Customer booking that service gets a video call link tied to their booking time
✅ Both customer and staff get a reminder with the video link before the appointment
✅ Video call works in-browser, no app download required for the customer
✅ Booking, payment, and reminders reuse the existing in-person flows

tasks.subject: Deeper analytics / multi-location reporting
tasks.description:
As a salon owner with multiple locations, I want performance rolled up across all locations and broken down by staff/service, so that I can make better business decisions.

Prerequisites:

Confirm the data model already links multiple locations under one owner account — may need a data-model change first

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Dashboard shows revenue, bookings, and retail sales broken down by staff member
✅ Dashboard shows top/bottom performing services by revenue and booking count
✅ Owners with multiple locations can view a combined "all locations" dashboard, and drill into a single one
✅ Reports are filterable by date range (this week/month/custom)
✅ Reports can be exported (CSV at minimum)

tasks.subject: Set up Meta Business Suite & apply as a Meta booking partner
tasks.description:
we need a verified Meta Business presence and (for the full in-app experience) approval as a Meta booking software partner, so that salons can offer "Book Now" on Facebook and Instagram.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Aspio has a verified Meta Business Manager account
✅ Aspio's own Facebook Page and Instagram Business account are linked inside Meta Business Suite
✅ Aspio has confirmed whether a formal Meta booking-software partner application exists for our category, and submitted it if so (this is what lets "Aspio" appear as a selectable tool in a salon's own Facebook/Instagram "Book Now" button setup, the way Square and Boulevard do today)
✅ We have documented Meta's approval requirements and rough timeline, so Phase 2 of ticket 8 can be planned realistically

tasks.subject: Book Now button — Facebook & Instagram
tasks.description:
As a salon owner, I want customers to book directly from my Facebook Page and Instagram profile, so that I don't lose leads who find me on social media.

Prerequisites:

Phase 1: none — standard profile feature, no approval needed
Phase 2: requires ticket 7 (Meta Business Suite + partner approval) to be complete

Acceptance Criteria 

✅ Salon owner can add a "Book Now" button to their Facebook Page linking to their Aspio booking page
✅ Salon owner can add a "Book" action button to their Instagram business profile linking to their Aspio booking page
✅ Instagram button only requires the account to be a Business account (not Creator) linked to a Facebook Business Page

✅ Aspio is registered as a bookable provider inside Meta Business Suite, so salons can select "Aspio" directly from Facebook/Instagram's native booking-button setup
✅ Customers can complete a booking without leaving Facebook/Instagram (native overlay), not just a redirect
✅ Bookings made via Facebook/Instagram appear identically in the salon's Aspio calendar

tasks.subject: Apply as a Reserve with Google partner
tasks.description:
We need to be an approved Google booking partner, so that salons can offer real-time booking directly in Google Search and Maps.

Prerequisites:

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ We have completed Google's Reserve with Google partner interest form
✅ We have a Google Cloud Platform project set up to access the Maps Booking API
✅ We have an SSH key pair generated for secure SFTP access to Google's feed dropbox
✅ We have confirmed our merchant/service eligibility against Google's criteria (physical address matching Google Maps data, standard service definition)
✅ We have a named Google Business Development contact or confirmed the self-serve partner path

tasks.subject: Reserve with Google , Google booking integration
tasks.description:
As a salon owner, I want customers to book directly from Google Search and Maps, so that I capture demand from people searching for salons nearby.

Prerequisites:

Phase 1: none — standard Google Business Profile feature
Phase 2:  (Google partner application) to be complete

Acceptance Criteria 

✅ Salon's Google Business Profile shows a "Book" link pointing to their Aspio booking page, via Google's own appointment-link setting

✅ Aspio implements a live availability feed, uploaded at least every 24 hours, covering all participating salons
✅ Aspio implements the required "Booking Server" API endpoints so Google can query availability and create bookings
✅ Aspio passes Google's sandbox review before requesting production access
✅ Customers can view real-time availability and book directly inside Google Search/Maps results

tasks.subject: Smart onboarding by business type
tasks.description:
As a new salon signing up, I want Aspio to pre-fill relevant service categories, services, and staff roles based on my business type, so that I can get set up quickly instead of starting from a blank page.

Prerequisites:

Content team needs to author starter category/service templates per business type before engineering can wire it up

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Signup flow asks the user to select their business type from a visual category picker
✅ Based on the selection, the system pre-fills a starter set of service categories and common services with suggested pricing/duration
✅ User can select more than one business type if they offer multiple kinds of services
✅ All pre-filled data is fully editable before the user finishes setup
✅ A typical single-location salon can complete onboarding (business type → contact info → business name → address → done) in under \~5 minutes

tasks.subject: Chatbot
tasks.description:
As a salon owner, I want an in-app chatbot to answer common setup and usage questions, so that I don't have to wait for human support for simple things.

Prerequisites:

Help/FAQ content must exist first — the chatbot is only as good as the content behind it
Decide build vs. buy (e.g. an off-the-shelf support-bot product vs. building on an LLM API directly)

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Chatbot is accessible from every page in the business portal (e.g. floating help button)
✅ Chatbot answers common questions about settings, features, and billing using existing help content
✅ Chatbot escalates to human support when it can't answer or the user asks for a person
✅ If escalated, the support team can see the chatbot conversation history so the customer doesn't repeat themselves

tasks.subject: AI website builder (design + color)
tasks.description:
As a new salon owner, I want Aspio to generate a ready-to-launch website for my business automatically.

Prerequisites:

Choose an AI provider/model for layout + color generation, and confirm expected per-generation cost against budget

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ During onboarding, the user provides a short business description (or reuses business type + name already entered)
✅ The system generates a complete website: layout, color palette, and a service menu pulled from their actual services
✅ The generated site is immediately live at the salon's Aspio website URL, and fully editable afterward in the existing website editor
✅ The user can regenerate a different design if they don't like the first result

tasks.subject: AI-generated service images
tasks.description:
s a salon owner without professional photos, I want AI to generate an image for each of my services, so that my listing doesn't look empty.

Prerequisites:

Choose an image-generation API provider and confirm its licensing terms allow commercial use in a public salon listing
Decide on a content-safety filter/review step before an image can go live

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ If a service has no uploaded photo, the system offers an AI-generated placeholder image matching the service name/category
✅ The salon owner can accept the AI image, regenerate a different one, or upload their own photo instead
✅ AI-generated images look like normal service photos to customers — no visible "AI-generated" label on the public listing

tasks.subject: AI-generated service & company text
tasks.description:
As a salon owner, I want AI to write my service descriptions and "About us" text, so that I don't have to write marketing copy myself.

Prerequisites:

Can likely reuse the AI provider/infrastructure chosen for ticket 13 — confirm before scoping separately

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ User can trigger AI text generation for a service description from a few inputs (service name, category, tone)
✅ User can trigger AI text generation for an "About us" / company bio from business type, name, and a couple of prompts
✅ Generated text is inserted as an editable draft — never published without the owner reviewing and confirming it
✅ User can regenerate if they don't like the result

tasks.subject: Multi-language support
tasks.description:
As a salon owner or customer who doesn't speak Swedish or English, I want to use Aspio in my own language, so that the product is usable for me.

Prerequisites:

Decide which languages/markets to prioritize first, recommend 1–2 target expansion markets rather than all at once
Confirm whether the current codebase already externalizes UI strings for translation, or needs an i18n refactor first
Decide translation approach: professional translation vs. AI-assisted with human review

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Business portal UI can display in at least \[N new languages, to be decided based on target markets]
✅ Consumer marketplace app UI supports the same set of languages
✅ Language selector is available and persists per user across sessions
✅ Customer-facing notifications (SMS/email reminders, confirmations) send in the customer's selected language
✅ New languages can be added without a full app re-release (translations stored separately from code)

tasks.subject: Customer Email Validation in Journal Loyalty
tasks.description:
Fix issues in the Journal Loyalty system where a single user can be associated with multiple customer records. Add email validation before upsert of customer data to ensure that each user maps uniquely to one customer.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ One user can only have one customer record.

✅ Duplicate customer creation blocked by email validation.

✅ QA confirms loyalty points and deals remain consistent.

tasks.subject: Correct Availability Rendering in Booking Page (Match Web Approach)
tasks.description:
Update the Aspio Business App booking page so that availability is displayed correctly. Currently, when a slot is selected, only that slot shows as available. The fix should ensure the booking page behaves like the web approach, showing all valid availabilities while highlighting the selected one.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Booking page shows all available slots.

✅ Selected slot is highlighted but does not hide others.

✅ QA confirms behavior matches web approach.

tasks.subject: Show Out‑of‑Hours Bookings on Calendar
tasks.description:
Update the Aspio Business App so that bookings made outside of configured working hours (e.g., 7 PM or 6 PM) are still visible on the calendar. Currently, bookings outside business hours may not display, which reduces visibility for staff and owners.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Out‑of‑hours bookings display on calendar.

✅ Bookings remain editable and manageable.

✅ QA confirms consistent behavior across roles and devices.

tasks.subject: AI Studio Memories & Data Integration in Nest Backend
tasks.description:
Integrate AI Studio memories and other related data into the Nest backend, ensuring that all required endpoints are ready for use. This will allow AI Studio to store, retrieve, and process memory data alongside other structured inputs for improved personalization and learning.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Endpoints for AI Studio memories and data are implemented.

✅ Data integration works seamlessly with existing backend collections.

✅ QA confirms memory persistence and retrieval accuracy.

tasks.subject: Update Aspio Business APK Backend Integration
tasks.description:
Update the Aspio Business APK so that the old Aspio Studio AI backend is replaced with the Business Web APIs for generation tasks, while saving operations are handled by the Nest backend. This ensures consistency with the web approach and improves reliability.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ APK uses Business Web APIs for generation.

✅ APK uses Nest backend for saving.

✅ QA confirms smooth functionality across all flows.

tasks.subject: Implement Three‑Layer Context in Nest Backend & APK
tasks.description:
Enhance the Nest backend and Aspio Business APK by implementing three distinct layers — Application, Categories, and Company — to provide structured context for AI features. These layers will be integrated with the APK so that the AI can leverage them for improved personalization, recommendations, and contextual learning.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Application, Categories, and Company layers implemented in Nest backend.

✅ APK integrated with backend endpoints for all three layers.

✅ AI Studio uses layered context for personalization.

✅ QA confirms smooth functionality across workflows.

tasks.subject: Improve Salon Identification in Loyalty Cards
tasks.description:
When navigating to Loyalty Cards, salon names are hidden because long addresses expand too much and push the names out of view. Users currently need to click on the salon name to see which salon it is. Update the UI so salon names are always visible and easily identifiable.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Salon names are always visible in loyalty card view.

✅ Addresses are truncated but expandable.

✅ QA confirms improved usability across devices.

tasks.subject: Add Short Descriptions for All features in Business App
tasks.description:
Enhance the Aspio Business App by adding short explanatory text for Deals and Loyalty Cards. These descriptions should help businesses understand the purpose, benefits, and current free‑to‑create status of these features.

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Deals section shows clear description text.

✅ Loyalty Card section shows clear description text.

✅ QA confirms readability and consistency across devices.

tasks.subject: Design UI/UX for Marketplace Review System
tasks.description:
Design the UI/UX for the Marketplace review system so that users can review companies based on the services they used. The design should provide a clear, intuitive flow for submitting reviews, displaying company ratings, and ensuring transparency for other customers.

Requirements:

Frontend (Marketplace App):

Create review entry points from booking history and company profiles.

Design review form with star rating (1–5), optional written feedback, and booking details.

Display reviews on company pages with verified booking badge.

Show aggregated ratings and distribution (average score, star breakdown).

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Users can submit reviews tied to services they booked.

✅ Reviews display with verified booking badge.

✅ Company ratings and responses are visible and consistent.

✅ QA confirms smooth review flow across devices.

tasks.subject: Design UI/UX for Marketplace Review System mobile view

tasks.subject: Background Processing for Completed/Cancelled bookings with Failure-Only Alerts

Acceptance Criteria:

✅ Implement optimistic UI updates so tasks immediately transition to completed or cancelled state upon user action without blocking the interface.

✅ Execute backend completion/cancellation API calls silently in the background without displaying global or local loading spinners, overlays, or success pop-ups.

✅ Suppress all success toast messages and success modals for task status changes.

✅ Implement error interceptors that listen for background network or server failures, reverting the UI state to its prior state if the operation fails.

✅ Trigger a clear error notification banner/toast only in the event of a background request failure to inform the user that the change could not

tasks.subject: Re-implement Schedule Service Pricing Logic & WordPress Booking Integration

tasks.subject: Backend: Unified Subscription Logic for Stripe & Telebirr (SAR Backend)

tasks.subject: Infrastructure & Core Module: Centralized NestJS Logger System

tasks.subject: Migrate Business App Logging to NestJS
